To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
3 genetic loci of the reninangiotensin system (angiotensinogen T235T, angio-tensinconverting enzyme D allele, and aldosterone synthesis C344T) are associated with nonmodulating hypertension.
the angiotensignogen M235T (235 TT), angiotensinconverting enzyme (DD), and aldosterone synthetase C−344T (−344 TT) genotypes identify a subset of patients with nonmodulating hypertension.

the angiotensignogen, angiotension-converting enzyme, aldosterone synthese genotypes identified individuals who had the nonmodulating hypertension phenotype, which is a subclass of essential hypertension with an increasing degree or fidelity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification and validation of genetic markers that can be used in the prediction of the nonmodulating hypertension phenotype.
the genetic determinants of essential hypertension and its intermediate phenotypes, such as the renin- angiotensin- aldosterone system (RAAS)–nonmodulating hypertension.
the genetic basis of the renin–angiotensin system (RAS) and the relationship between RAS genes and blood pressure (BP) regulation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

angiotensin converting enzyme DD genotype in association with the 235TT genotype of the angiotensigen gene, and the −344 TT genotype of the CYP11β2 gene, can identify a subgroup of patients with essential hypertension that is characterized by a nonmodulating phenotype.

the combination of 235 TT and 235 TT, 235 TT, or 235 TT and C−344 TT genotypes at the angiotensionogen and aldosterone synthases genes, respectively, can be used as surrogate markers for predicting the nonmodulator phenotype.

the combination of the angiotensingen 235 TT, aldosterone synthasen 344 TT, and angiotensinen 235 TT, and angio- converting enzyme D/D genotypes can predict the presence of the nonmodulating hypertension phenotype with a specificity and sensitivity of 100% and 80.7% and an OR of 5.36.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

genetic variation in the renin-aldosterone-angiotensine system can identify a subclass of essential hypertension with a nonmodulating phenotype and that this phenotype can be predicted with increasing fidelity as additional genetic variants of the renin– angiotensin- aldosterone system are included in the genetic profile.

the angiotensins and aldosterone are the major determinants of blood pressure in the general population, whereas the adrenocorticotropic hormone–adrenal axis is the major determinant of blood pressure in a subset of hypertensives with nonmodulating hypertension.
the angiotensinegn 235 TT genotype and the aldosterone synthase −344 TT genotype can identify individuals with the non-modulating phenotype with a 2-fold increase in the odds.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the angiotensins are the key to the hypertension puzzle.

the combination of the angiotensininogen M235T and angiotensinin-converting enzyme I-D polymorphisms can predict the non–angiotensin II modulating phenotype in essential hypertension, with an odds ratio of 3.74.
there is a genetic component to hypertension, and this can help in determining the most effective treatment.
